label: rem:adelic-substrate-integration
title: Motivation for the adelic substrate and Tate integration
html:
Motivation for the adelic substrate. Replacing \mathbb{R} by \mathbb{A} resolves a structural tension already noted in classical limit (preamble): the local q-geometries at each prime do not assemble into a continuous manifold, but they do assemble into a global adelic object. The macroscopic universe is therefore not the real continuum \mathbb{R} alone but the simultaneous integration of all local non-archimedean data weighted by their archimedean shadow.

Adelic integration (Tate's thesis). Global observables of the substrate — the macroscopic mass functional, the global L-function of Bring's coordinate ring, the partition functions of the brane tower — are not Riemann integrals over \mathbb{R}. They are Tate integrals over \mathbb{A}:

  \mathcal{Z}(s)
  \;=\;
  \int_{\mathbb{A}^\times} \! f(x)\,|x|^s\, d^\times x
  \;=\;
  \zeta_\infty(s) \cdot \prod_{p} \zeta_p(s),

a product of local zeta integrals, one per place. The classical \zeta(s) of classical Riemann zeta is recovered as the global Tate integral of the standard adelic Schwartz function. Local q-zeta data and macroscopic real-valued observables are two faces of the same adelic object.

Discrete quantum data at every prime is glued by adelic restriction and projected to physical numbers by the archimedean realization functor.
